name: First 3-Second Dynamic Zoom Hook
use_when: A feed-first short needs immediate motion, proof, face, or curiosity before the viewer swipes.
The opener has a speaker, proof artifact, image stack, or emotional subject that can receive a simple zoom.
The first line is strong but the opening frame feels static.
avoid_when: The zoom would crop the face, proof, product, captions, or action that makes the hook understandable.
The hook claim is unsupported by the rest of the short.
The format intentionally starts with a still, meditative, or long-form invitation beat.

timeline_pattern.first_seconds_rule: In feed-first shorts, the first 3-5 seconds should contain a visual reason to keep watching.
timeline_pattern.proof_rule: Pair the motion with a concrete image, proof frame, or face whenever possible so the zoom is not empty motion.
timeline_pattern.focus_rule: Name the viewer's first focal point before choosing zoom direction.
timeline_pattern.support_rule: The dynamic hook improves chances of attention only when the content, story, and payoff can support the opening.

motion.rule: Use a simple scale/position move that lands quickly and holds the focal point.

keyframe_values.hook_window: Place the main motion or proof entry inside the first 3-5 seconds.
keyframe_values.subtle_talking_head_scale: Start around 103-112% or end there for a gentle push/pull when the face must stay natural.
keyframe_values.stronger_proof_scale: Use roughly 115-130% only when the source resolution, crop, and proof visibility remain safe.
keyframe_values.move_duration: Try 12-30 frames for crisp social motion; use a slower 1-3 second move when the story wants calm.
keyframe_values.hold_after_move: Hold at least 8-18 frames after the move lands so the viewer can read the face or proof.

sound.rule: Use no SFX, a low whoosh, or a tiny hit depending on tone; the first words must stay clear.

captions.rule: Opening captions should not cover the zoom target or proof frame.
captions.avoid: Do not stack hook text, captions, and proof images so densely that the focal point disappears.

color.rule: The first frame should reveal the subject or proof clearly; avoid dark or muddy frames unless mystery is intentional.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use zoompan or crop/scale expressions for the first 3-5 seconds, then render a phone-size contact sheet to check proof and caption safety.
implementation.remotion: Create a hook sequence with startScale, endScale, focusBox, proofLayerFrame, and holdFrames fields.
implementation.blender: Use camera scale/position keyframes aimed at a face or proof plane; ease into a short hold.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Apply keyframes or Dynamic Zoom to the first clip and add the proof/image layer before the spoken hook finishes.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Motion or Transform keyframes on the first shot or adjustment layer, align to safe guides, and check that the proof frame remains visible.

common_mistakes: Adding a dynamic zoom to a weak or unsupported hook.
Cropping away the proof or face that should carry attention.
Letting ordinary captions cover the first proof frame.
Using so much motion in the opener that the viewer cannot parse the premise.
Repeating the same zoom direction in every short until it feels automatic.
qc: Does the first 3-5 seconds give a clear visual reason to keep watching?
Can the viewer identify the first focal point immediately?
Does the zoom preserve faces, captions, proof, products, and action?
Does opening audio stay intelligible during the motion?
Is the hook supported by later proof, story, or payoff?
